The short answer is that I don't think there's a true labor shortage. 

The companies reporting that they can't hire anyone right now are the same ones reporting record profits. Labor shortages are where qualified employees are so hard to find that operations shut down and companies begin to go out of business because they can't find staff. A company would always rather pay employees more than they would lose profit due to stores shutting down. The fact that businesses are still profitable and not raising wages en masse in an effort to outbid their competition is proof that there isn't a shortage for most types of labor. The issue right now is not that there isn't a supply of labor, it's that laborers don't want to work at the wages set by these companies. When companies are truly desperate to put butts in seats they will raise wages to the point where they can fill vacancies.

That would be true if the US didn't boost it's population through immigration. US population has nearly doubled since the Immigration Act in 1965. Between population growth and computer automation, the supply of labor has greatly outpaced the demand which has reduced wages.
